title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals scale-dependent fault controls at Gonghe geothermal site
summary: A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site. The catalog resolves a ring-shaped distribution with four clusters and varying faulting styles. The authors infer that site-scale seismicity reactivated mapped, pre-existing natural faults; at borehole scale, the principal seismogenic zone coincides with strong SHmax rotation. Stress modeling estimates a low fault-friction coefficient near 0.23 (95% CI 0.19–0.48) and the low-to-moderate fluid overpressure needed for slip.
ai_technology: Machine-learning earthquake-detection and cataloging workflow (model details are not stated in the publisher abstract)
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; Institute of Geomechanics, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences; ETH Zürich

evidence.tested: A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site.
evidence.unknown: The source checked here is the original publisher abstract and plain-language summary. The catalog is observed, while fault reactivation, chlorite-rich gouge consistency, stress controls and required fluid overpressure are the authors’ interpretations/model estimates, not direct causal proof. No claim is made that the AI model alone establishes these mechanisms.
evidence.ai_role: The authors state that machine learning was used to detect earthquakes and compile the high-precision 7,346-event catalog; the resolved spatial pattern supplies the seismicity observations used in their scale-dependent fault-structure interpretation and stress analysis.
